subject.title: fix(process): trim UTF-8 boundary on win32 in truncated command output

question: Should truncated Windows command output remain byte-preserving for non-UTF-8 command encodings, or should OpenClaw explicitly normalize Windows capture to UTF-8 before UTF-8 boundary trimming?
rationale: The patch changes a platform-specific compatibility boundary, and source-level mocked tests cannot determine the intended contract for real Windows shell and tool output.

options.title: Preserve arbitrary Windows bytes
options.body: Keep the Windows bypass unless capture has already been explicitly normalized to UTF-8, preserving existing legacy-codepage command output.

options.title: Adopt UTF-8-only capture
options.body: Define and implement explicit Windows UTF-8 normalization before truncation, document the compatibility change, and prove it against native Windows command output.

recommendation.title: Preserve arbitrary Windows bytes
recommendation.body: Keep the Windows bypass unless capture has already been explicitly normalized to UTF-8, preserving existing legacy-codepage command output.

likelyOwner.reason: The original guard appears to date to the Execa refactor, but the contributor and reviewer history could not be safely resolved in the restricted read-only environment.
